title: Adaptive Reservation Intake: negotiated throughput SLAs, autoscale policy templates, and fleet entitlement controls
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Goal: Build a single, operational reservation intake workflow that supports negotiated throughput SLAs, exposes a set of canonical autoscale policy templates, and implements fleet entitlement controls for Dedicated customers. This ticket captures the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for the intake form, approval lanes, and capacity planning guidance used by sales/CS/solutions teams.

Why this matters: Sales and Customer Success are frequently negotiating committed throughput instead of pure on-demand usage. Current intake forms are ad-hoc and force engineering to do manual sizing. We need a predictable, auditable process that: (1) lets us specify throughput SLAs with optional burst policies, (2) maps SLA terms to autoscale / capacity guardrails, and (3) surfaces deployment-level constraints (region, VPC requirements, fleet entitlements) to the provisioning queue. This reduces onboarding time, prevents overcommit, and enables measurable revenue recognition.

Scope (what's in):
- New reservation intake UI fields and API: negotiated target RPS/Tokens-per-second, burst allowance, preferred regions, compliance flags, and billing commitment window.
- Approval lanes: auto-approve low-risk requests; manual review for >X committed units or non-standard regions. Approval matrix ties to quota/finance limits.
- Autoscale policy templates: latency-first, cost-first, hybrid. Each template maps to fleet sizing heuristics, min/max replicas, cold-start budget, and fallback variant rules.
- Fleet entitlement controls: tag-based entitlements + enforced route-level quotas; operators can pin fleet pools to customers during probation.
- Cost & capacity estimator: back-of-envelope run rate and 12-month forecast integrated into intake form (pre-approval).
- Integrations: GitHub PRs for infra changes, Confluence runbook, Console dashboard for reservations and active commit telemetry.

Out of scope (this ticket):
- Dedicated billing contract generation (handled by Finance).
- On-prem air-gapped installer changes beyond metadata flags.

Open trade-offs and decisions to make: 
- Minimum guaranteed throughput vs. percent-of-peak guarantees (engineering prefers percent-of-peak for elasticity; sales prefers fixed guarantees for SLA clarity).
- Autoscale template granularity: 3 canonical templates vs. policy DSL. Start with 3 templates to reduce complexity and iterate to a DSL in a follow-up.
- Approval thresholds (ops vs sales-driven) — propose ops owns >500k committed tokens/mo review.

Acceptance criteria (must be all true to call Done):
acceptance_criteria: Intake form (UI + API) captures negotiated throughput, burst allowance, region, compliance flags, and billing window
Approval lanes implemented with auto-approve rules and manual review flow; audit log entries for every decision
Three autoscale policy templates implemented and wirematched to runtime autoscaler config
Capacity estimator returns a 12-month run rate and suggested fleet sizing for chosen template
Console shows reservation dashboard with committed vs observed throughput and projected run rate
Ops playbook (Confluence) for approving/pinning fleets and decommit procedures published
End-to-end smoke test that simulates a reservation, approval, and automated fleet pinning succeeds in staging
